dossier.purpose: Difftastic (binary `difft`, written in Rust) is a command-line structural diff tool for human review. It detects each file's language, parses both versions with tree-sitter, diffs the simplified syntax trees (Dijkstra shortest path over a graph of syntax positions) and prints syntax-aware changes (side-by-side or inline; an unstable JSON mode also exists). It falls back to a line-oriented diff with word highlighting for unsupported languages, oversized inputs, graph-limit overruns and, by default, any parse error. It is wired in as an external diff command for git, Mercurial, Fossil and Jujutsu. Non-goals stated by the README: generating patches and merging (README.md:10-11, 59-73; src/main.rs:605-858).

claims.claim: Difftastic is a structural diff tool that compares files based on their syntax.
The README has no install commands; it defers to the manual's Installation page.
Not line-oriented: 'If you reformat your code and it's now split over multiple lines, difftastic will show you what's actually changed.'
Compatible with git (configuration instructions in the manual) 'as well as many other version control systems'; also usable with mercurial.
Supports 'over 30 programming languages'; a file with an unrecognised extension gets a line-oriented diff with word highlighting.
Known issues: scales 'relatively poorly on files with a large number of changes' and 'can use a lot of memory'; side-by-side display 'can be confusing'; 'regularly has releases that fix crashes'.
Non-goal, patching: output is 'intended for human consumption' and does not generate patches that can be applied later.
Non-goal, merging: AST merging is not addressed (the README points elsewhere for merges); AST diffing is lossy with respect to whitespace.
By default falls back to a line-oriented diff on parse errors so it 'never claims that two syntactically different files are the same'; DFT_PARSE_ERROR_LIMIT allows a small number of errors.
Since 0.50 a single file containing conflict markers can be passed and difftastic diffs the two conflicting sides.
'Difftastic always considers order to be important'; unordered data such as JSON keys must be sorted beforehand.
`difft --check-only --exit-code before.js after.js` checks whether two files have the same AST without computing a diff ('much faster'); exit code 0 means no syntactic changes, 1 means changes.
Integration with other tools: 'Probably not. Difftastic is young.'; Emacs users can use magit or difftastic.el.
License: MIT; the vendored tree-sitter parsers in vendored_parsers/ are 'a mix of the MIT license and the Apache license' (see vendored_parsers/*/LICENSE); sample_files/ are MIT unless stated.

install.command: Download the archive for your OS/CPU from https://github.com/Wilfred/difftastic/releases/latest and extract the `difft` executable (release assets are named difft-<version>-<target>.tar.gz on Unix; no shell command is documented)

install.method: Cargo from source (crates.io); needs Rust >= 1.85 and a C++14 compiler

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - release builds exist for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-musl (.github/workflows/release.yml:29-30, 38-39) and both are in the CI test matrix (.github/workflows/test.yml:14, 24). The gnu binaries are built on ubuntu-22.04, so they need a correspondingly recent glibc (CHANGELOG.md:199-203).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - README, manual and CI never mention WSL. A Linux x86_64 binary is published (release.yml:29-30), but WSL2 itself is neither documented nor tested.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - aarch64-apple-darwin is built natively in the release workflow (release.yml:33-34) and tested natively on macos-14, an M1 runner (test.yml:20-21); `brew install difftastic` is documented (manual/src/installation.md:16-23).
platforms.gpu: no - not used or required; CPU-only Rust CLI with no GPU dependency (Cargo.toml:39-139). The only 'CUDA' hit is a file-extension comment (src/parse/guess_language.rs:259).

integrations.cli: yes - the `difft` binary (Cargo.toml:161-163). Usage `difft [OPTIONS] OLD-PATH NEW-PATH` (src/options.rs:26); also two directories, `-` for stdin, a single file with conflict markers, and the 7/9-argument GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF form (src/options.rs:909-1011; manual/src/usage.md:8-58). Flags: --display {side-by-side, side-by-side-show-both, inline, json}, --exit-code, --check-only, --ignore-comments, --skip-unchanged, --sort-paths, --override, --override-binary, --list-languages, --byte-limit, --graph-limit, --parse-error-limit, --dump-ts/--dump-syntax/--dump-syntax-dot (src/options.rs:152-381); most have DFT_* env vars (manual/src/usage.md:60-69). Exit codes 0/1/2 (src/exit_codes.rs:1-12; manual/src/usage.md:84-94). VCS wiring documented for git (diff.external, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, difftool; other git commands need --ext-diff), Mercurial extdiff, Fossil diff-command and Jujutsu ui.diff-formatter (manual/src/git.md:14-139, mercurial.md:3-28, fossil.md:3-13, jj.md:3-13).
integrations.mcp: none found - no MCP server, config or mention in the README, manual, src/ or workflows (searched the checkout excluding fixtures).
integrations.sdk_or_api: none found - binary-only crate (Cargo.toml:161-163, no [lib]), no HTTP API; internal rustdoc is published but not on docs.rs (manual/src/contributing.md:47-53). The only machine-readable interface is the CLI's `--display=json`, which is refused unless DFT_UNSTABLE is set (src/options.rs:812-819; src/display/json.rs:296-314).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: none found - no Claude Code or Codex plugin, skill, hook or documentation. AGENTS.md:1-3 only tells AI contributors to follow AI_POLICY.md and not to edit CHANGELOG.md unless asked; AI_POLICY.md:4-12 requires understanding the code, disclosing AI use, and human-written issue/PR comments.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics or phone-home found. src/ has no network code: the only URLs are comments and the --help footer text (src/options.rs:123-139), and Cargo.lock contains no HTTP/TLS/async-runtime crates (reqwest, hyper, ureq, tokio, openssl, rustls, native-tls all absent). No account or network service is required at run time. The only subprocess is `git check-attr diff binary -z -- <path>`, run for each diffed file and ignored if git is unavailable (src/gitattributes.rs:26-74; src/main.rs:420-424); build.rs also runs `git log -1` when .git exists (build.rs:88-109). Binary detection reads the local system MIME database when present (manual/src/from_source.md:30-43). Logging is local, via DFT_LOG/pretty_env_logger (src/main.rs:144). CI-only network use: Codecov upload (.github/workflows/coverage.yml:19-23), curl download of the typos binary (test.yml:122-123), GitHub Pages deploy (deploy_docs.yml:56-62).

languages: C (vendored tree-sitter parsers compiled by build.rs via the cc crate)
Markdown (mdBook manual under manual/ and translation/zh-CN/)

entry_points.what: fn main(): initialises the DFT_LOG logger, calls options::parse_args() and dispatches Mode::{Diff, DiffFromConflicts, ListLanguages, DumpTreeSitter, DumpSyntax, DumpSyntaxDot, GitHasUnmergedFile}; binary name `difft` (Cargo.toml:161-163)
clap CLI definition app(); parse_args() at :725 maps 2/7/9-argument forms (git external-diff protocol, :909-958) and DFT_* environment variables
diff_file() (read, text/binary/encoding detection, .gitattributes check) and diff_file_content() at :605 (language guess, tree-sitter parse, unchanged pre-pass, Dijkstra, fallbacks, hunks)
diff_directories(): rayon-parallel directory diff; results printed serially, sorted (--sort-paths) or collected for JSON
print_directory() / print(): the unstable JSON output (directory mode prints an array, two-file mode prints one object)
build script: compiles 4 vendored C parsers (janet-simple, kotlin, latex, smali), embeds git commit date/hash and rustc version, sets JEMALLOC_SYS_WITH_LG_PAGE=16
23 assert_cmd integration tests that drive the built `difft` binary
output-regression runner: builds release, diffs every sample_files/*_1.* pair, md5s the output into compare.result and compares it with compare.expected

code.architecture: Single Rust binary crate (no [lib]). Pipeline driven from src/main.rs: src/options.rs (clap + DFT_* env) -> src/files.rs (file/stdin//dev/null reading; text-vs-binary and encoding heuristics: valid UTF-8, UTF-16 with BOM, near-UTF-8, Windows-1252, MIME type via tree_magic_mini; directory walk with the `ignore` crate, hidden files included, .git excluded, lines 277-284) and src/gitattributes.rs (`git check-attr diff binary`; the 0.69 changelog says it honours '-text' and 'binary' but the code reads the `diff` and `binary` attributes) -> src/parse/guess_language.rs (language from --override globs, Emacs mode header, shebang, Hack/Objective-C heuristics, filename globs, `<?xml`; 65 Language variants) -> src/parse/tree_sitter_parser.rs (per-language TreeSitterConfig: atom nodes, delimiter tokens, ignorable trailing tokens, highlight queries, embedded sub-languages such as JS in HTML; converts the tree-sitter tree to the simplified atom/list Syntax of src/parse/syntax.rs and counts parse errors against the limit) -> src/diff/ (unchanged.rs pre-pass that shrinks the problem; graph.rs + shortest_path.rs Dijkstra over lazily built vertices bounded by DFT_GRAPH_LIMIT; sliders.rs post-processing; changes.rs ChangeMap; lcs_diff.rs Histogram diff via imara-diff for lines and words) -> src/display/ (hunks.rs, context.rs, side_by_side.rs, inline.rs, json.rs, style.rs). The plain-text fallback is src/line_parser.rs + src/words.rs. src/conflicts.rs rebuilds the two sides of a conflict-marker file; src/summary.rs holds DiffResult/FileFormat; src/exit_codes.rs holds the 0/1/2 codes. Grammars: 58 crates.io parser crates (Cargo.toml:82-139) plus 4 vendored C grammars under vendored_parsers/ (symlinked *-src dirs built by build.rs; manual/src/parser_vendoring.md:19-41). jemalloc is the global allocator except on Windows, illumos and FreeBSD (src/main.rs:102-107).
code.packaging_and_release: Source: crate `difftastic` on crates.io, published by the release workflow with katyo/publish-crates and the CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN secret (.github/workflows/release.yml:67-74). Binaries: pushing a tag matching [0-9]+.* creates a draft GitHub release (taiki-e/create-gh-release-action, release.yml:3-21) and uploads difft-<tag>-<target> archives (.tar.gz on Unix, .zip on Windows, built with --locked) for x86_64/aarch64 Linux gnu, x86_64 Linux musl, x86_64/aarch64 macOS and x86_64/aarch64 Windows MSVC via taiki-e/upload-rust-binary-action (release.yml:23-65). The version in the filename is new in 0.71 (CHANGELOG.md:29-32); 0.70 fixed binaries that ignored Cargo.lock (CHANGELOG.md:60-64). No checksum, signature, SBOM or provenance/attestation step is configured in any workflow (a search of .github/ for attest, cosign, sigstore, sha256, checksum, provenance, slsa, gpg and sign finds nothing); whether the third-party upload action emits checksum files by default cannot be determined from this checkout. No workflow declares `permissions:`. Other upstream artefacts: man page difft.1 generated from difft.1.md (manual/src/packaging_difftastic.md:53-59), cargo-deb metadata (Cargo.toml:165-173), cargo-binstall metadata pointing at the release archives (Cargo.toml:33-37; not mentioned in the docs), mdBook manual + rustdoc + homepage deployed to GitHub Pages on pushes to master (deploy_docs.yml:1-62). Distro packages (Homebrew, Arch, Nix, Fedora, FreeBSD, winget, Scoop, Chocolatey) are third-party (manual/src/packaging_difftastic.md:6-8; manual/src/installation.md). Docs reference ./scripts/release.sh (manual/src/contributing.md:84-94) but no such file exists in this checkout. CHANGELOG.md:1 still reads '0.71 (unreleased)' at the 0.71.0 tag, so the tag date is not determinable here.
code.tests_and_ci: Rust built-in harness: 124 #[test] functions in 19 src files with #[cfg(test)] modules (e.g. src/parse/guess_language.rs, src/diff/unchanged.rs, src/display/context.rs) plus 23 integration tests in tests/cli.rs (assert_cmd + predicates; exit codes, binary override, --check-only, --ignore-comments, directory and git-style arguments, parse-error fallback) = about 20 test-bearing Rust files and 147 tests. One test is #[ignore]d because it needs the system MIME database (src/files.rs:374-378); CI runs it with `cargo test -- --ignored` (test.yml:53-61). No test covers --display json (no 'json' in tests/; no #[test] in src/display/json.rs). Output-regression fixtures: about 109 before/after pairs (sample_files/*_1.* vs *_2.*) whose md5-hashed output is compared with sample_files/compare.expected (sample_files/compare_all.sh:28-43). CI workflows in .github/workflows: test.yml (on push and pull_request) runs `cargo test` on 7 targets (Linux x86_64 gnu/musl, aarch64 gnu via cross, macOS arm64 native and x86_64 via cross, Windows x86_64 and arm64) with Rust 1.85.0, the MIME-DB tests, a latest-stable test, the output-regression diff, `cargo package --allow-dirty`, rustfmt, actionlint and typos (test.yml:5-125); coverage.yml uploads cargo-llvm-cov results to Codecov with fail_ci_if_error false and informational project status (coverage.yml:17-23; .codecov.yml:5-11); deploy_docs.yml and release.yml as described above. No clippy step (clippy.toml exists), cargo-audit/cargo-deny, or Dependabot/Renovate configuration in the checkout.
code.dependencies: Single Cargo.toml (no workspace). [dependencies]: 88 direct crates, of which 30 are general (clap, regex, rayon, serde/serde_json, tree-sitter, tree-sitter-language, tree_magic_mini, ignore, imara-diff, strsim, encoding_rs, ...; Cargo.toml:40-79) and 58 are tree-sitter language-parser crates (Cargo.toml:82-139). Plus 1 target-specific (tikv-jemallocator, :143), 3 dev-dependencies (assert_cmd, predicates, pretty_assertions; :145-149) and 3 build-dependencies (cc, rayon, version_check; :151-156). Cargo.lock has 175 [[package]] entries including the root crate (root entry at Cargo.lock:202) and no HTTP/TLS/async-runtime crates. The 4 vendored grammars carry their own Cargo.toml/package.json, but only their src/*.c files are compiled (build.rs:44-65). Toolchain: Rust >= 1.85 (Cargo.toml:21; rust-toolchain.toml:2) plus a C/C++ compiler (manual/src/from_source.md:3-10); optional system MIME database (manual/src/from_source.md:30-43).
code.security_policy: none - no SECURITY.md or equivalent anywhere in the checkout; .github/ holds only ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md and four workflows. Unrelated to vulnerability reporting, AI_POLICY.md:1-12 sets rules for AI-assisted contributions (understand and disclose AI use; issue and PR comments must be human-written) and AGENTS.md:1-3 points AI contributors to it.

claim_checks.claim: Structural diff: difftastic 'compares files based on their syntax' and shows what actually changed even after reformatting (README.md:10-11, 31-33).
claim_checks.evidence: diff_file_content() guesses the language (src/main.rs:621), parses both inputs with tree-sitter (src/main.rs:658-668; src/parse/tree_sitter_parser.rs:1296-1320), converts them to a simplified atom/list tree that stores no whitespace (src/parse/tree_sitter_parser.rs:1594-1639; manual/src/parsing.md:28-34, 93-97), pre-marks unchanged subtrees (src/diff/unchanged.rs:19-34) and runs Dijkstra over ordered syntax positions (src/main.rs:693-718; src/diff/shortest_path.rs:59-130; src/diff/graph.rs:19-46). Files that differ only in non-significant whitespace print 'No syntactic changes.' (src/main.rs:928-930). Caveat: blank-line and whitespace changes are invisible by design (manual/src/tricky_cases.md:437-457).

Understated; the code wins. The Language enum has 65 variants (src/parse/guess_language.rs:21-87) and the manual table lists 62 rows: 52 programming-language and 10 structured-text (manual/src/languages_supported.md:11-62, 68-77). 58 crates.io parser crates plus 4 vendored C parsers back them (Cargo.toml:82-139; build.rs:44-65). Markdown has no entry in the language globs (src/parse/guess_language.rs:196-427), so .md files take the line-diff fallback. Detection order: --override globs, Emacs mode header, shebang, Hack/Objective-C heuristics, filename globs, `<?xml` header (src/parse/guess_language.rs:469-516).

claim_checks.claim: Unrecognised extensions and parse errors fall back to a line-oriented diff (README.md:46-47, 95-99).
claim_checks.evidence: No guessed language -> line_parser::change_positions (src/main.rs:646-655), a Histogram line diff with word-level matching inside novel lines (src/line_parser.rs:108-126; src/diff/lcs_diff.rs:1-8, 34). The parse-error limit defaults to 0 (src/options.rs:22, 357-368) and to_syntax_with_limit() rejects any tree with more errors (src/parse/tree_sitter_parser.rs:1575-1589), triggering the fallback labelled 'Text (N <lang> parse errors, exceeded DFT_PARSE_ERROR_LIMIT...)' (src/main.rs:754-796; src/summary.rs:23-32). Files over --byte-limit (1,000,000) or graphs over --graph-limit (3,000,000) fall back the same way (src/options.rs:17-21; src/parse/tree_sitter_parser.rs:1314-1317; src/main.rs:720-729, 799-821). Nuance: detection is not extension-only; shebang, Emacs header and `<?xml` also select a language.

claim_checks.claim: `--check-only --exit-code` sets exit code 0 for no syntactic changes and 1 for changes, and is 'much faster' (README.md:155-168).
claim_checks.evidence: Exit codes 0/1/2 and the --exit-code gate are as described (src/exit_codes.rs:1-12; src/main.rs:391-396). Check-only returns before the graph diff (src/main.rs:670-691) and compares syntax trees by content id, ignoring positions (src/parse/syntax.rs:614-621); trailing-comma lists compare equal (src/parse/syntax.rs:652-663). But for unsupported-language files and every fallback (parse errors, byte limit) check-only compares raw text, so any byte difference counts as a change (src/main.rs:578-603, 649-651, 783-791, 808-816); binary files report byte changes (src/summary.rs:55-65). 'Much faster' is never quantified (CHANGELOG.md:899-901) and cannot be checked from the repo.

claim_checks.claim: Not in the README: the CLI help and man page say `--display json` outputs 'a machine-readable JSON array with an element per file' (src/options.rs:218-226; difft.1.md:64).
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from the help text. JSON requires DFT_UNSTABLE and is called 'an unstable feature' whose 'format may change' (src/options.rs:812-819; the man page omits this). Two-file mode prints a single object, not an array (src/main.rs:386; src/display/json.rs:308-314); only directory mode prints an array (src/main.rs:319-324; src/display/json.rs:296-306). The schema is per-file {aligned_lines, chunks[lines{lhs/rhs{line_number, changes[{start, end, content, highlight}]}}], language, path, status} (src/display/json.rs:186-266), i.e. token spans within lines with highlight kinds delimiter/normal/string/type/comment/keyword/tree_sitter_error, not function- or class-level entities. By code reading (not executed): --check-only leaves positions and hunks empty (src/main.rs:679-690) so json status would be 'unchanged' (src/display/json.rs:64-83), and json with a conflict-marker file reaches `unreachable!()` (src/main.rs:266, 990). No test covers JSON.

claim_checks.claim: Compatible with git 'as well as many other version control systems' (README.md:37-39).
claim_checks.evidence: Git external-diff protocol with 2, 7 and 9 arguments including renames and mode changes (src/options.rs:909-958), /dev/null for added/removed files (src/options.rs:488-506), unmerged-path handling (src/options.rs:885-899), git temp-file naming (src/options.rs:606-621). The manual documents git, Mercurial, Fossil and Jujutsu (manual/src/git.md, mercurial.md, fossil.md, jj.md; manual/src/usage.md:3-6). Caveat: git <= 2.43.1 can crash with an external diff when file permissions change (manual/src/git.md:6-10). Other git commands need --ext-diff (manual/src/git.md:26-40).

claim_checks.claim: Output is 'intended for human consumption' and difftastic 'does not generate patches' (README.md:61-63).
claim_checks.evidence: The only display modes are side-by-side, side-by-side-show-both, inline and json (src/options.rs:211-227); no unified/patch output exists and the diff result is positions and hunks for rendering (src/summary.rs:35-53).

claim_checks.claim: Performance 'scales relatively poorly on files with a large number of changes, and can use a lot of memory' (README.md:51-52).
claim_checks.evidence: Consistent with the code, which bounds the cost with defaults of 1,000,000 bytes per file, 3,000,000 graph vertices and 0 parse errors (src/options.rs:17-22), falling back to a line diff when exceeded (src/main.rs:720-729, 799-821). The graph-limit comment says it was chosen so a pathological sample terminates in about 5 seconds (src/options.rs:18-21); the manual notes graph-traversal bugs can cause huge memory use (manual/src/profiling.md:11-12). No benchmark numbers are published.

claim_checks.claim: Difftastic 'regularly has releases that fix crashes' (README.md:57).
claim_checks.evidence: CHANGELOG.md has 33 lines mentioning crash or panic across its history, but the most recent explicit 'crash' wording is in 0.62 (CHANGELOG.md:244-246); sections 0.63 to 0.71 (CHANGELOG.md:1-240) contain none, although 0.68 fixed 'fatal: external diff died' for unmerged paths (CHANGELOG.md:98-101).

claim_checks.claim: License is MIT, and vendored parsers are 'a mix of the MIT license and the Apache license' (see vendored_parsers/*/LICENSE) (README.md:195-200).
claim_checks.evidence: Root license is MIT (LICENSE:1; Cargo.toml:6). Vendored kotlin, latex and smali have MIT LICENSE files (vendored_parsers/tree-sitter-kotlin/LICENSE:1, tree-sitter-latex/LICENSE:1, tree-sitter-smali/LICENSE:1). vendored_parsers/tree-sitter-janet-simple has no LICENSE file and an empty license field (package.json:12; its Cargo.toml has no license key). No Apache-licensed parser directory exists; Apache appears only in highlight-query headers derived from nvim-treesitter (vendored_parsers/highlights/latex.scm:1, hcl.scm:1, cmake.scm:1; vendored_parsers/tree-sitter-kotlin/queries/highlights.scm:1).

risks: Machine-readable output is unstable and thin: --display=json is refused unless DFT_UNSTABLE is set and 'its format may change in future' (src/options.rs:812-819); it is absent from the README and manual (only --help, the man page and CHANGELOG.md:557-558 mention it) and no test covers it (tests/cli.rs; src/display/json.rs). Two-file mode emits an object while the help says array (src/main.rs:386 vs src/options.rs:226). By code reading (not executed), --check-only with json reports status 'unchanged' (src/main.rs:679-690; src/display/json.rs:64-83) and json with conflict-marker input reaches unreachable!() (src/main.rs:266, 990).

Scope and granularity: output is per-line token spans with highlight kinds (src/display/json.rs:214-266), not entities such as functions or classes, and it is explicitly not patch-applicable or mergeable (README.md:59-73). The tool compares two inputs only; it has no GitHub/PR/API, worktree, MCP, agent or evaluation features and no network code (searched README, manual, src/ and workflows).

Silent degradation to a line diff: any tree-sitter parse error (default limit 0), more than 1,000,000 bytes per file, or more than 3,000,000 graph vertices switches to a line diff (src/options.rs:17-22; src/main.rs:720-821); the downgrade is visible only in the file header or the JSON `language` value, 'Text (...)' (src/summary.rs:23-32). The README itself lists poor scaling, high memory use and crash-fix releases as known issues (README.md:49-57).

Syntactic equality hides some changes: whitespace and blank lines are not stored (manual/src/parsing.md:93-97; manual/src/tricky_cases.md:437-457 says this 'can hide accidental code reformatting'); trailing commas are ignored for Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, Rust, Swift and TypeScript (CHANGELOG.md:68-73; src/parse/syntax.rs:652-663); CR characters are stripped by default (src/options.rs:261-269); --ignore-comments exists. With --exit-code such differences return 0 in supported languages.

Release and supply-chain hygiene: no checksums, signatures, SBOM or attestations are configured; no workflow declares `permissions:`; dtolnay/rust-toolchain is referenced by tag or branch rather than SHA (.github/workflows/test.yml:34, 59, 69, 78, 90, 99; deploy_docs.yml:31); CI downloads the typos binary with curl and no checksum (test.yml:122-123); there is no SECURITY.md, Dependabot/Renovate config, cargo-audit/deny or clippy step; 175 locked packages including 58 third-party parser crates built with a C toolchain (Cargo.toml:82-139; Cargo.lock).

Maintenance and documentation drift: single listed author (Cargo.toml:8); parsers abandoned upstream have been dropped (Hare, Elvish, SCSS, Hack: CHANGELOG.md:23, 50-51, 84-85); tree-sitter is capped below 0.26.11 because of solidity and `ignore` below 0.4.30 for MSRV (Cargo.toml:51-54, 74-78); 0.66 was skipped over a release-process issue and 0.70 fixed binaries that ignored Cargo.lock (CHANGELOG.md:60-64, 157-160); manual/src/contributing.md:89-91 references a scripts/release.sh that does not exist; CHANGELOG.md:1 still says 0.71 is 'unreleased' at the 0.71.0 tag; the README says 'over 30' languages while the code has 65 (src/parse/guess_language.rs:21-87).

Licensing: the root license is MIT (LICENSE:1), but vendored_parsers/tree-sitter-janet-simple has no LICENSE file and an empty license field (package.json:12), unlike kotlin, latex and smali (MIT LICENSE files). The README's 'MIT and Apache' description of vendored parsers (README.md:198-200) does not match the tree, where Apache is cited only in highlight-query headers (e.g. vendored_parsers/highlights/latex.scm:1).

Platform and runtime dependencies: binary-vs-text detection uses the system MIME database when present (manual/src/from_source.md:30-43; src/files.rs:174-213); a `git check-attr` subprocess runs per diffed file and is silently skipped if git is missing (src/main.rs:420-424; src/gitattributes.rs:26-74); git <= 2.43.1 can crash with an external diff when permissions change (manual/src/git.md:6-10); Linux gnu binaries are built on Ubuntu 22.04, which sets a glibc floor (CHANGELOG.md:199-203); source builds need Rust >= 1.85 and a C/C++14 compiler (manual/src/from_source.md:3-10); WSL2 is neither documented nor tested.
